claim: A staff work-order in the U.S. Department of Justice's Epstein file production — a "Zorro Ranch Projects / Tasks List" dated 4/4/01 from Jeffrey Epstein's roughly-10,000-acre New Mexico ranch in Stanley — logs that ancient petroglyph rocks were relocated onto the property's grounds. Two entries read "3/29 Petroglyph rocks moved to the main house" and "3/30 One rock has been brought up and placed in the old dog yard. JE to let us know the size, location and how many rocks he would like." Petroglyphs are stone carvings of archaeological and tribal significance; removing them from public or tribal land is regulated under federal antiquities law. The document records the movement of the rocks on the ranch and Epstein's direction over the collection; it is a primary record from the DOJ release.
